title: Switch to a new broadband package
intent: An existing customer moves to a different package on the same line.

screens.purpose: The customer sees what they could move to, and picks one.

props.heading: Choose a new package
props.explain: You can change package once a month. Your line stays connected throughout.

annotations: Emphasis on Family is a business decision, not a design one — it is the most-switched-to package.
Nothing here knows the customer's address yet, so every package is shown whether or not it is available.

screens.purpose: The customer confirms the line can carry the package they chose.

props.heading: Check your line
props.explain: We need your postcode to confirm the speed we can deliver.

props.message: We will check this against the exchange before you confirm.

annotations: This is the screen the postcode-first variation moves to the front. If the chosen package turns out to be unavailable here, the customer has already invested in a choice we then take away.

screens.purpose: The customer adds optional services before committing.

props.heading: Anything else?
props.explain: You can add or remove these later without changing your contract.

annotations: Skip and Continue reach the same screen. Whether that is two actions or one is a journey question, and a good example of something the sketch should make arguable.

screens.purpose: The customer confirms who they are and how to reach them.

props.heading: Your details
props.explain: We will use these to confirm the switch and tell you when it happens.

annotations: In the postcode-first variation the address is already known here, so this screen is shorter.

screens.purpose: The customer reviews everything and commits.

props.heading: Check and confirm
props.explain: Your new package starts on the next billing date.

annotations: Every row here reaches back into the journey. A design system with no answer for an inline edit affordance will show up as an escape hatch on this screen first.
